page: Amazon Web Services r8a.metal-48xl is a bare-metal memory-optimized instance featuring 192 dedicated physical x86_64 cores powered by AMD EPYC 9R45 processors clocked up to 4.5 GHz. The configuration operates with one thread per core without simultaneous multithreading overhead. Memory allocation reaches 1,536 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 RAM, providing 8.0 GB of system memory per core. The server includes 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, while integrated local storage is absent, requiring external network-attached volumes for data persistence.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate exceptional parallel computation and memory throughput. The system achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core CPU testing (702,043.61) and Geekbench multi-core workloads (26,822.0), supported by instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16. Memory read bandwidth registers at 1,039.86 GB/sec on uncached large-block transfers, complemented by 430.64 GB/sec write bandwidth. In-memory data throughput is equally elevated, showing 439.2 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and top-tier PassMark database operation scores.

From an infrastructure investment perspective, r8a.metal-48xl delivers high core density and substantial memory capacity in a unified, non-virtualized physical platform. The bare-metal design eliminates hypervisor contention, providing predictable execution times across extensive parallel batch jobs. However, the lack of local NVMe storage requires high-throughput network storage architectures to avoid input/output bottlenecks when processing persistent datasets.

This instance profile fits large-scale in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, extensive electronic design automation, large Clang compilation matrices, and CPU-driven machine learning inference models requiring vast memory footprints.
description: Amazon Web Services r8a.metal-48xl is a bare-metal memory-optimized server powered by 192 dedicated physical AMD EPYC 9R45 cores running at 4.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture without SMT, it incorporates 1,536 GB of DDR5 system memory operating at 6 GHz, offering an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. The server features 75 Gbps baseline networking and contains no local storage, relying on external network volumes. Benchmark testing confirms top-tier multi-threaded processing, reaching 702,043.61 on stress-ng and 26,822.0 on Geekbench multi-core. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth exceeds 1,039 GB/sec, driving exceptional performance in Redis operations at 439.2 million operations per second. Hardware support includes AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 capabilities. AWS r8a.metal-48xl is structured for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, in-memory caching tiers, large database instances, and distributed batch processing.
